title: Reduce observability tail overhead with sampled-span proxy and compact metrics encoder
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce CPU and memory overhead caused by our current observability pipeline under high QPS. Work includes introducing a low-overhead sampled-span proxy for hot paths, replacing high-cardinality metric encoders with a compact delta-based encoder, and upgrading OpenTelemetry SDKs to the latest stable with the zero-allocation exporters where possible.
background: Recent SRE incidents and continuous profiling showed the observability path contributes up to 18% additional CPU at fleet p90 during request storms. We currently use an in-process OTLP exporter with synchronous batching, high-cardinality metric encoders, and liberal span attributes on request hot paths. Previous refactors (see ENG-44122 and ENG-46688) reduced allocations but we still see tail latency regressions correlated with trace flushes and metric serialization spikes.
proposal: 1) Introduce a sampled-span proxy that keeps full span data for debug sampling but forwards lightweight sampled headers for the common 99% path. 2) Replace the JSON metric encoder used in some services with a compact delta encoder (protobuf-lite + label intern pool) to reduce allocations and bytes on the wire. 3) Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK to latest stable (version 1.x.x) and enable the new async exporter and span-shipping buffer. 4) Add a feature flag and canary rollout that toggles the proxy and encoder independently per service. 5) Add litmus tests and perf benchmarks to CI and a post-deploy dashboard to measure regressions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P95 CPU contribution from observability path reduced by >=40% in synthetic high-QPS load test
P99 request tail latency due to observability flush reduced by >=30% in canary cluster
Memory allocations per request for trace/metric codepath reduced by >=50% in service-level profiler
No increase in dropped spans beyond baseline (<=1% delta) when sampled-span proxy is enabled
Feature flags exist to disable proxy or encoder per-service and per-region
E2E integration tests and perf bench automated and passing in CI

progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Spike completed — microbenchmarks show that compact delta encoder is ~3x faster on serialization and reduces encoded size by ~60% for typical metric batches (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/compact-metrics-spike)

2025-02-24: Prototype sampled-span proxy implemented for runtime-go and validated with unit tests. Prototype reduces span-path allocations by ~70% in a synthetic path (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6123)

2025-02-28: OTEL SDK upgrade branch opened; initial test run in staging caught incompatibility with older exporter configuration — working on migration shim (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-config/pull/97)
2025-03-02: Canaries prepared in staging cluster. Added CI perf job that runs bench-suite after test deployment and fails on >10% regression (CI job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/obs-perf-master)
2025-03-04: Running 10% prod canary for sampled-span proxy in us-west-2 (metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/observability-pipeline?orgId=1&var-cluster=canary)
Notes: Spike and early canary show reduced CPU and allocation counts but increased dropped span rate in one legacy component — tracked as follow-up
review_feedback: PM Owen: approve canary as long as feature-flagged and with 24h rollback guard
Security (SLA Team): requested KMS key usage review for proto encoder artifacts — assigned to Rahul
SRE: prefer sampled-span proxy to be opt-in per service to avoid surprising telemetry gaps; require a fallback to full-span submission on elevated error rates
Design: suggested telemetry schema changes to differentiate proxy-sampled spans from full spans for downstream analytics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Sampling could hide production regressions. Mitigation: Keep a deterministic debug sampling rate that retains full spans for a fixed subset of requests and route those to long-term storage
Risk: OTEL upgrade may break older exporters. Mitigation: Maintain a temporary compatibility shim and run migration in staging for 48h before prod rollout
Risk: Compact encoder may lose labels if intern pool collides. Mitigation: Use strong hashing and reconciliation test in CI
Risk: Can cause short-term spike in network egress. Mitigation: Rate-limit initial canary and monitor egress metrics closely
monitoring_signals: observability.cpu_pct_by_service (board) — expected drop for instrumented services
post_deploy_checks: Verify no increase in ERROR logs from exporter component for 72h
Run 'perf-verify' CI job against canary for two 12-hour windows
Confirm APM profiler snapshots show allocation reductions
Confirm downstream analytics ingesters receive expected number of full spans (taking sampling into account)
